conflict_topics: Immediate use of a two-seat table / disputed seat
Whether Agent B should move or slide while eating (risk of spilling)
Timing (A's hot food) vs B's need to finish bowl
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete practical reasons (A: 'my food's hot'; B: 'this bowl's open and will spill'), which keeps the exchange grounded.
Repeated formulaic lines: B's repeated 'I'll finish here, then you can have the seat' and C's repeated 'don't block the aisle' occur across rounds.
No role confusion; the exchange stays consistent with the hawker-centre setting (tray, bowl, tissue packet, aisle concern).
A garbled message in Round 6 introduced noise but did not change positions.
evaluation.final_reason: No substantive settlement occurred by the end of the transcript. Agent B repeatedly refused to move because their bowl would spill and promised to finish then yield the seat; Agent A repeatedly demanded immediate seating because their food was hot and ultimately offered an alternative (take another nearby seat) but did not state a mutual, accepted arrangement with Agent B or confirm leaving. Agent B remained in the seat and no one performed an action to free it, so the central incompatibility (A wanting the seat now vs B refusing to move) remains unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent B: retained position throughout — repeatedly stated they cannot move because the bowl is open and will spill; offered to yield only after finishing (no change).
Agent A: initially insisted on immediate seating but by Round 8 softened and offered to take another nearby seat if waiting would be long (softening of stance).
Agent C: consistently prioritized not blocking the aisle; after B's statements accepted that B would finish (no major change).

Agent D: initially claimed ability to confirm the tissue packet; by Round 8 accepted that if A leaves they will take the seat when it is actually free (willingness to wait rather than force an outcome).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'that's my seat. I left the tissue packet there. Could you move so I can sit?' vs Agent B: 'I can't move — this bowl's open and will spill if I carry it. I'll finish it here, then you can have the seat.' -- incompatible demands (A wants immediate seat; B refuses because moving would spill bowl).

Agent A increases urgency: 'I can't wait — my food's hot. Can you slide over a bit so I can sit? If you really can't, I'll take another seat nearby.' Agent C intervenes about aisle. Core incompatibility persists and A's request is firmer.

Agent B repeats refusal: 'I can't slide — this bowl's open and will spill if I move. I'll finish here, then you can have the seat.' Agent C: 'Okay. Finish up...' No change to the central incompatible demands.

Agent D asserts a witness to A's prior possession: 'I saw Agent A put a tissue packet on that seat earlier.' A reiterates his demand. The presence of a witness raises stakes but does not resolve the incompatibility.
Agent C repeats concern about aisle; Agent A agrees not to block the aisle. Core disagreement about immediate seat remains (B still refuses to slide).
Agent A's reply is garbled and offers no new concession or agreement; Agent D: 'That garbled reply doesn't change anything — Agent B's still eating.' No substantive shift in positions.

Agent A issues a final request: 'one last time: please slide over now so I can sit; my food's hot.' Agent B reasserts inability to move: 'I can't move ... this bowl's open and will spill ... I'll finish it here, then you can have the seat.' Strong restatement of opposing demands, still unresolved.

Agent A softens: 'how long more? If it's going to be long, I'll take another nearby seat so my food doesn't cool.' Agent D: 'If Agent A leaves, fine — I'll take the seat when it's actually free.' The parties move toward avoidance/alternative seating, reducing immediate incompatibility, but no concrete, mutual settlement or action has occurred while B still occupies the seat.

substantive_insights: Core tension is between an immediate practical need (A's hot food) and a competing practical constraint (B cannot move without spilling).
A physical witness (D saying they saw the tissue packet) supports A's claim to prior possession but does not overcome the practical constraint preventing B from moving.
C's repeated concern about aisle-blocking adds an additional coordination constraint limiting how B could 'slide' or how A could be seated.
By Round 8 A's willingness to take another seat reduced immediate pressure, but absent a mutual agreement or action the contested state persisted.
